items.stem: Distinguish between a receipts and payments account and an income and expenditure account.
items.answer: R&P summarises actual cash received and paid (capital and revenue); I&E records income and expenditure of the period on the accruals basis, showing a surplus or deficit.
items.markingKey: R&P – cash, all items [1]; I&E – accruals, revenue items, surplus [1] [2]

items.stem: Explain why members of a club need an income and expenditure account as well as a receipts and payments account.
items.answer: The R&P account does not show whether the club covered its running costs in the year; the I&E shows the true surplus or deficit after accruals and depreciation.
items.markingKey: R&P shows only cash [1]; I&E shows surplus/deficit [1] [2]

items.stem: Explain why subscriptions received in advance are not income of the current year.
items.answer: They relate to membership of a future year; under the accruals concept they become income in the year they cover, so they are a liability now.

items.stem: Explain why a club might not include subscriptions in arrears in its income.
items.answer: Members who have not paid may have left and never pay; prudence suggests recognising them only when received.

items.stem: Explain why a club uses the terms surplus and deficit instead of profit and loss.
items.answer: A club exists to provide facilities for members, not to make a profit; a surplus simply means income exceeded expenditure.

items.stem: Explain how the accumulated fund at the start of the year is calculated.
items.answer: From the opening statement of affairs: total assets (equipment, inventory, bank, arrears, prepayments) less liabilities (payables, accruals, advances).

For the year its income was: subscriptions $9,840, competition fees $2,850, bar profit $1,180; expenditure was: rent $7,960, coaching $2,960, general expenses $700; depreciation of equipment was $1,720. (a) Calculate the accumulated fund at 1 January. (b) Calculate the accumulated fund at 31 December.

Greenfield Cricket Club runs a bar. For the year: bar sales $9,310; payments to bar suppliers $4,080; bar inventory $1,640 at the start and $1,900 at the end; amounts owing to bar suppliers $830 at the start and $1,120 at the end. The bookkeeper calculated the bar profit as $5,490. Identify the error and state the correct bar profit.
items.answer: Payments to suppliers were used as purchases without adjusting for the amounts owing at the start and end of the year. Correct bar profit: $5,200.
